title: Publishing platforms' labelling policies

sources.title: TikTok Newsroom, Partnering with our industry to advance AI transparency and literacy (9 May 2024)
TikTok Community Guidelines, Integrity and Authenticity: Edited Media and AI-Generated Content
Meta Newsroom, Labeling AI-Generated Images on Facebook, Instagram and Threads (6 February 2024)
Meta Transparency Center, Labeling AI Content
Meta Help Center, How to identify AI content on Meta products
YouTube Help, Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content
Google, How we're increasing transparency for gen AI content with the C2PA (17 September 2024)
Google My Ad Center Help, AI transparency in ads

rules.title: TikTok: label realistic AI content when you post it
rules.summary: TikTok requires creators to label AI-generated or significantly edited content that shows realistic-looking scenes or people. Unlabelled content may be removed, restricted or labelled by TikTok.
rules.quote: we require creators to label AI-generated or significantly edited content that shows realistic-looking scenes or people

rules.title: TikTok labels content that carries Content Credentials
rules.summary: TikTok reads Content Credentials on upload and labels images and videos that carry them as AI-generated automatically.
rules.quote: TikTok is starting to automatically label AI-generated content (AIGC) when it's uploaded from certain other platforms
rules.unverified: What TikTok shows for a signer that is not on the C2PA trust list, and whether marks survive its re-encode, is not stated; we are measuring it.

rules.title: Meta: label photorealistic video and realistic audio
rules.summary: On Facebook, Instagram and Threads, Meta may require an AI label on photorealistic video and realistic-sounding audio that was digitally created or altered, and may penalise content shared without one. Images are exempt from the duty, though Meta may label them anyway.
rules.quote: Meta may require an AI label when content has photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio that was digitally created, modified or altered, including with AI.

rules.title: Meta labels marked content "AI Info"
rules.summary: Meta labels images "AI Info" when it detects industry-standard indicators, including the C2PA and IPTC metadata that a signed manifest carries.
rules.quote: These labels are now displayed as 'AI Info'
rules.unverified: Whether the manifest and watermark survive in the file after upload, and what Meta shows for an untrusted signer, are not stated; we are measuring them.

rules.title: YouTube: disclose realistic AI content in the upload flow
rules.summary: YouTube requires creators to disclose when AI meaningfully alters or generates photorealistic content, by answering the "AI use" question in YouTube Studio. Disclosing does not limit reach or earnings; repeatedly not disclosing can lead to a label, removal or Partner Program suspension.
rules.quote: we require creators to disclose when they use AI to meaningfully alter or generate photorealistic content

rules.title: YouTube labels uploads that carry C2PA metadata
rules.summary: YouTube may label content containing C2PA metadata automatically, and a creator cannot remove a label that C2PA metadata triggered.
rules.quote: content made with YouTube's AI tools, content with C2PA metadata, or content labeled after manual review cannot be adjusted

rules.title: Google Search shows AI origin in "About this image"
rules.summary: If an image carries C2PA metadata, searchers can see in "About this image" (Google Images, Lens and Circle to Search) whether it was created or edited with AI.
rules.quote: If an image contains C2PA metadata, people will be able to use our 'About this image' feature to see if it was created or edited with AI tools

rules.title: Google Ads: declare AI-generated creatives
rules.summary: For ad creatives made outside Google's own tools, the "How this ad was made" disclosure is the advertiser's own declaration: label AI-generated or edited assets when you upload them.
rules.quote: An advertiser can choose to label and disclose an asset as AI generated or edited
rules.unverified: Trade press reports visible on-ad labels as mandatory in the EU, India and New York; Google's own page does not say so.

rules.title: LinkedIn shows Content Credentials, including who issued them
rules.summary: Images and videos with Content Credentials get a C2PA icon on LinkedIn; clicking it shows whether AI was used, the app or device, the creator, the issuer and the date. The issuer is whoever signed the manifest.
rules.quote: The icon will be visible to all viewers of your content.
rules.unverified: Which trust list LinkedIn checks, and what it shows for a signer that is not on the C2PA trust list, are not stated.

changelog: 2026.10.12: first version, from the /labels pages as read 12 October 2026. A platform rule's effective_from is the date we read the policy: it is in force at least since then; the pages do not give start dates.
